hook: A fire lookout, a trapdoor in its ceiling, and another identical lookout above: the premise is simple, and the article gives you time to settle into it. It's built from expedition logs, so expect slow climbing and creeping unease rather than early action. Glance at the object class line and the revision date in the procedures before you start.
whyItMatters: 3333 sits in the endless-space tradition alongside SCP-087, but leans into the idea that whatever you're exploring may be studying you in return. Its dry procedural voice, describing a situation that keeps getting worse, makes it a good model of slow-burn horror in the format. A late speech about height and enlightenment gives it a thematic layer beyond the scares.
thingsToNotice: The doubled class and a task force created after the logs are a quiet spoiler that the expeditions did not stay contained. Watch how trust erodes: base camp keeps pushing people upward, and later the question becomes whether the voices on the radio belong to who they claim. Small details, like a nickname someone would never use, turn out to be decisive. The empty summit reads as a comment on our habit of expecting answers at the top. The final log is the most graphic part of the article, so go in prepared.

related.note: The classic endless stairwell, explored downward with a similar sense of being watched.
Another endless building whose apparent staff are not what they seem.
